name: Dehydrated Skin
description: Dehydrated skin lacks moisture and appears dull, flaky, or rough. It is distinct from oily or dry skin types and requires a targeted approach to address its specific needs.
characteristics: Does not respond well to harsh products

morning_routine.action: Cleanse with a gentle, hydrating cleanser.
morning_routine.purpose: Remove impurities without stripping the skin's natural barrier.

night_routine.action: Cleansing and toning to remove dirt and excess oils.
night_routine.purpose: Prep the skin for overnight hydration and repair.

night_routine.action: Apply a hydrating serum or moisturizer rich in hyaluronic acid, glycerin, or aloe vera.
night_routine.purpose: Lock in moisture and provide intense hydration throughout the night.

weekly_care: Use a hydrating mask to deeply nourish and replenish skin.
lifestyle_tips: Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water daily.
Use a humidifier to add moisture to indoor air during dry seasons or climates.
common_mistakes: Over-exfoliating the skin, which can strip it of its natural oils and worsen dehydration.
Using heavy, occlusive products that can clog pores and lead to breakouts.
do: Use a humidifier during dry seasons or climates to keep your indoor air from becoming too dry.
Incorporate hydrating masks into your weekly skincare routine for an extra boost of moisture.
dont: Skip moisturizing, as this can exacerbate dehydration and make the skin more susceptible to environmental stressors.
Use products that contain alcohol or fragrances, which can further dry out the skin.

seasonal_care.summer: Increase your sunscreen usage to protect against UV damage, which can dehydrate the skin. Use a lightweight, oil-free moisturizer with SPF during hot weather.
seasonal_care.winter: Use heavier, richer moisturizers and lip balms to combat cold air and indoor heating that can strip moisture from the skin.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Be cautious of water-based products as they can wash away natural oils; opt for thicker, hydrating formulas.

expert_tips: Consider using a hyaluronic acid-based product as it can hold up to 1000 times its weight in water, providing long-lasting hydration.
Regularly check the ingredients list of your products and avoid those that include harsh chemicals or preservatives known for dehydrating the skin.
